newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: APEC calls for WTO financial services pact.
newsitem.headline: APEC calls for WTO financial services pact.

text.p: Asia-Pacific finance ministers of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum called on Sunday for the resumption of this month's World Trade Organisation's (WTO) financial services talks, and urged WTO members to agree to commitments on improving market access.

The APEC communique, released as the ministers wound up their weekend meeting at a luxury resort island hotel, also noted that major misalignments in exchange markets that existed in the spring of 1995 had been corrected.
That is something the powerful Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations also said at their meeting in February, and could be seen as an endorsement of exchange rates roughly around current levels.

They said three "key and closely intertwined" challenges facing the economically diverse APEC nations were to secure freer and stable flows of capital, facilitate private sector investment in infrastructure projects and the development of financial and capital markets.

An estimated $1.5 trillion will be needed in the next decade to build telecommunications links, roads and other core infrastructure in the region, and APEC needs to lure the private sector for the funds.
But the group fell short of making any binding commitments in order to tackle these challenges, calling most of the initiatives "voluntary principles," and giving no time frame for implementation.
On policy coordination, APEC noted that interdependence of member economies and financial markets are increasing, and agreed to enhance policy cooperation where appropriate.

The fund flow proposals centre around more uniform regulation among members, transparency and availability of information, easing the ability to invest internationally and liberalising financial markets.

The ministers also adopted recommendations from a private sector business advisory council -- from the establishment of regional information centres on financing needs to creation of bond rating agencies.

"This validates the utility of the APEC process. If the nations of APEC move forward with these recommendations...you will have made a very real contribution to developing the infrastructure for capital market development," U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said.

APEC comprises Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan, Thailand and the United States.
